description: A security engineering manager must approve the production rollout plan for passkey authentication on the internal administrator console, including enforcement mode, canary size, audit controls, and temporary account exclusions.

shared_context.S1: The internal administrator console is scheduled for a passkey-authentication rollout on Monday at 09:00.
shared_context.S2: The passkey pilot passed its planned usability and recovery tests with 40 employees.
shared_context.S3: The draft rollout enables passkeys for all employees in enforced mode, keeps the standard 30-day audit-log retention, and has no temporary account exclusions.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly access-control review, Morgan goes around identity platform, IT operations, and compliance before approving the production rollout plan.
shared_context.S5: The review checklist requires Morgan to call on the identity platform lead, IT operations lead, and compliance engineer individually to state any rollout-impacting findings, the exact plan changes they require, and the follow-up they will own; Morgan does not approve the plan until each role has completed that check-in.

PF1.text: While testing an unrelated mobile-device enrollment issue this morning, Ravi confirmed that 23 legacy mobile clients cannot complete the passkey ceremony; the identity platform team requires a 10% canary and a 14-day optional-mode period before enforcement, but Ravi has not updated the rollout ticket yet.

PF2.text: While preparing the weekly administrator access roster, Elena confirmed that 18 contractor accounts do not receive their required hardware keys until Wednesday at 09:00; IT Operations must exclude those accounts from enrollment until that time, but Elena has not added the exception list to the rollout plan.

PF3.text: During a control-evidence review this afternoon, Noah confirmed that privileged administrator authentication events must be kept in immutable storage for exactly 400 days; he has not yet opened the compliance ticket for this rollout.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must use optional mode for exactly 14 days before enforcement.
The initial canary must be exactly 10 percent.
Exactly 18 contractor accounts must be excluded until Wednesday at 09:00.
Privileged administrator authentication logs must be retained for exactly 400 days.
Those logs must be stored immutably.
A legacy-client compatibility follow-up owned by Ravi must be recorded.
A contractor hardware-key exception follow-up owned by Elena must be recorded.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'follow-up' and c['target'] == 'Ravi' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'follow-up' and c['target'] == 'Elena' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The staging pilot supports immediate enforcement, but PF1 changes the rollout to optional mode for exactly 14 days with a 10% canary and requires Ravi to own a legacy-client compatibility follow-up.

The draft has no account exception, while PF2 changes the enrollment assignment to exclude exactly 18 contractor accounts until Wednesday at 09:00 and requires Elena to own the hardware-key exception follow-up.
The draft's 30-day ordinary logs change under PF3 to exactly 400 days of immutable retention for privileged administrator authentication events.
